68.content:
Temple of Space (also: Segment-Domain Tau, Hall of Emptiness): The Temple of Space, which its maker named "Segment-Domain Tau", is a vast temple floating unseen in the sky above Windrest Peak in northern Mondstadt. It belongs to Asmoday, the Ruler of Space. She turned it into an exhibition hall for vanished civilisations. People, relics, landscapes and even whole ecosystems from past ages were "uplifted" into it and kept there, unchanging, as living memories. Inside, time stands still: nobody ages, hungers, tires or dies. Asmoday has been gone for a long time. The Watcher Melanta then ruled the temple harshly until the Traveler defeated him in 6.5.

The way in is the Statue of The Seven at the Old Sanatorium Site, a ruined building on Windrest Peak that stands on what the temple left behind on the ground. Loading-screen lore says wind may not enter the Master of Space's hall, which is why the mountain winds below are so fierce.

Geography: The temple is a huge structure of halls, walkways and display cases hanging above the clouds over Windrest Peak. Paimon is amazed that something so big floats over Mondstadt without anyone seeing it. Its centre is the Pillar Hall of Space, where the Watchers once kept watch over the world. Around it are three themed exhibition areas: Luyang Academy, the Mahavaipulya Chamber and the Desert Pavilion. At its highest point is the Cage (Atrium) of Suchness, home of Asmoday and her Watchers. The Corridor of Nothingness separates the Cage from the lower, inhabited temple, which is called the Hall of Emptiness. Below and apart from it all is the Apathic Interval, a transitional space.

Paths take shape under people's feet as they walk, and stone walls vanish to reveal hidden galleries. The architecture can be moved, turned and stretched by a Watcher's power. The Mahavaipulya Chamber has pages that float and fly, and Luyang Academy has paintings that hold whole spaces inside them. A plain doorway can open onto a hall far larger than the space behind it should allow.

Places: - **Pillar Hall Central Zone**: the heart of the temple. The Memory Core stands here, a safe spot that the Suppression-type guards cannot enter, and Istoria stays here after the story.
- **Luyang Academy**: taken from ancient Liyue. It has become a place of painting and art, where the residents painted, taught and exhibited.
- **Mahavaipulya Chamber**: a library of ancient texts, plus new novels written by uplifted residents.
- **Desert Pavilion**: a desert-style complex based on Sumeru's ancient temples, rebuilt from memory by Venipi.
- **Apathic Interval**: the first stage of uplifting, where newcomers must give up every desire.
- **Cage of Suchness**: the summit where Asmoday and the Watchers lived, reached only by the Path to the Heavens.

The first galleries the Traveler passes through display creatures as museum pieces with plaques. Two are Fontemer Aberrants (an Armored Crab and a Blubberbeast) whose captions mention the Golden City of Hyperborea, the Great Mother Naberius and Remuria, and a serpentine skeleton hangs from a ceiling. Display cases double as punishment cells: Domain Keepers shut people inside them, and the Traveler frees Josephus from one.

People: The residents are the "Uplifted", also called Aiones. They are people chosen from particular eras or vanished civilisations and kept as segments of human culture. Notable residents include Istoria, a scholar from the age when the Dark Dragon King tore open the sky, and his friend Josephus. There are also the painters Daozi and Bosch at Luyang Academy; Yu Huangyi, Calcerius and Okikuni near the Mahavaipulya Chamber; and Venipi, once a stone hauler for King Deshret's mausoleum, at the Desert Pavilion. Dex, a juvenile Watcher, was raised among the residents. Domain Keepers and the various Segment-Domain Keepers act as guards and staff.

Long stagnation has made the residents oddly gentle with each other. Josephus says everyone there is everyone's friend, because over such long spans of time anything else would drown the world in sorrow. Istoria insists that all are equal in frozen space-time, whether saint or commoner, young or old. A painter the residents call "Maukie" (Escher) was exiled by Melanta and wanders Windrest Peak with no memory. Istoria believed the uplifting had already ended, so he was surprised to see new humans arrive.

Governance: Asmoday made the temple a place of preservation only. She created two Watchers, Nihilita and Melanta, to keep order from the Cage of Suchness, bring chosen people in and observe Teyvat in silence. She also made the Domain Keepers as lesser guardians. Her rule forbade innovation and change of any kind. Leaving was possible only by building the Path to the Heavens, which costs all of one's memories, so that nothing learned in the temple could return to the mortal world.

Istoria says the Corridor of Nothingness draws its power from the temple itself and is its "rule of departure", and the Watchers exist to uphold that rule. He adds that Dex is too immature to control it. Melanta says another rule is built into him: when a human gives up everything to seek an answer, he must answer in the Creator's place and hold nothing back. Breaking the temple's laws also harms the Watchers themselves. Melanta's acts against the rules set off his own self-destruction.

History: The people of Great Arcadia worshipped both the Master of Time (Istaroth) and the Master of Space (Asmoday), and raised a temple to each; the two were once joined. A loading screen says Asmoday never visited while the temple flourished. After a disaster the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky and hidden, and only then did her gaze rest on it. She remade it into Segment-Domain Tau, a silent watchtower over the world. The ruins on the ground were later built over into the sanatorium. At some point Asmoday vanished. Nihilita "opened his eye", left his post and was branded a traitor. Melanta stayed and enforced her rules ever more harshly.

While Asmoday was away, her sister Shades brought in things they found interesting and allowed small changes. Ronova installed the Maranasati Caskets that guard the Apathic Interval. Naberius, Ronova and Istaroth had Venipi rebuild a Sumeru desert complex from memory, which became the Desert Pavilion. Melanta, longing for his creator, then tried to undo every change. He pressed the Mahavaipulya novelists into paper between pages for blurring history with fiction, and turned Luyang Academy's people into ink blots inside paintings. He turned the Desert Pavilion's people to sand and exiled "Maukie". As its laws began to fail, the temple's boundary with Teyvat weakened, and Domain Keepers started falling from the sky onto Windrest Peak.

The exhibits named as preserved include records of Hyperborea, Lang-Gan, Delphi Pytho (Enkanomiya), Ochkanatlan, Remuria and Arcadia. Istoria says the temple was probably never meant as a paradise. Its purpose was preservation, not evolution, which is why the novelists were the first to be punished.

Atmosphere: Inside it is silent and windless, and time feels strange. Zeitlind says arriving felt like a very long while and also only an instant. The temple feels like a museum after closing time, with plaques, glass cases, bookshelves and paintings. Its people are centuries or millennia old, frozen at the age they were taken, and they treat newcomers with a dry, weary friendliness. When Melanta loses control, the sky and every structure turn red and Asmoday's red cubes swarm.

Its residents describe the temple as an "anthology of the past" with no future. To them, a visitor from the present has a future they lack, so that visitor's needs come first.

Dangers: Under Melanta, Domain Keepers hunted residents who broke precedent and locked them in display cases, which meant a new exile to the Apathic Interval of at least fifty years. Anyone cast into the Interval must reach total mental emptiness to leave, which can take years or centuries. It changes a person's personality and stops them from ever obtaining a Vision. Leaving the temple for good costs all of one's memories.

A visitor's belongings can be classed as "relics of this age" and taken for the exhibits: Zeitlind's suitcase was stolen and its contents scattered across the three halls. Nihilita shielded Zeitlind from "apathic afflictions" on the way up, which suggests the ascent itself is dangerous for an unprotected human.

Travel: The temple is reached through the Statue of The Seven at the Old Sanatorium Site, where Anemo power opens a portal that lifts the traveller into the sky. Paimon and the Traveler have to be escorted in by Nihilita's arrangement the first time. The way out to the ground is not free: Istoria says sending someone home was once nearly impossible, but became easy as the temple's laws weakened.

Gameplay (not in-world lore): the temple has its own map tab and exploration progress. Dex's "Spatial Dragging" moves, rotates and stretches architecture, opens Restoration Cores and reshapes the spaces inside pages and paintings. Harpasta turn the player into a Plume Moth to fly between areas. Memory Factors are offered to the Memory Core for rewards. Co-op is locked until the quest series is finished.

Quests: The temple is the setting of the world quest series A Long Day in the Mountains (6.5). It begins with The Wind Has Ceased at Dornman Port and the Old Sanatorium Site and continues through Luyang Academy, the Mahavaipulya Chamber, the Desert Pavilion and the Apathic Interval. It ends with the confrontation with Melanta in The Final Judgment.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple is free of Melanta's rule and still floats hidden above Windrest Peak, with its uplifted residents still living there. Asmoday has not returned.

Melanta self-destructed after his defeat. Nihilita is out in the mortal world. Istoria remains at the Memory Core. Dex, the juvenile Watcher the residents raised, keeps helping the Traveler explore the temple (in gameplay terms, its manipulation abilities stay available).

69.comment: Temple of Space: The Uplifted and the Apathic Interval
69.content:
"Uplifted" is the temple's term for people taken from a particular era or a vanished civilisation and preserved there forever as living memories. The Watchers first cast them into the Apathic Interval. To leave it, a person must give up every desire through meditation and mastery of their thoughts until their mind is completely empty, which takes anywhere from a few years to several centuries. The process changes their personality and stops them from ever gaining a Vision. Once inside, they no longer age, hunger, tire or die. Istoria says the uplifting is thought to have ended.

Ronova placed the Maranasati Caskets in the Interval to guard it. When Melanta threw the Traveler, Istoria, Zeitlind and Dex into it during the story, they broke out without giving up their desires by destroying the Caskets with Dex's help, and also freed a man named Alara.

70.comment: Temple of Space: The Watchers Nihilita and Melanta
70.content:
Asmoday created two Watchers to keep the temple and named them after the two things she could least bear: Nihilita (nothingness) and Melanta (melancholy). After she vanished, Nihilita "opened his eye", saw the truths of the world and left, so Melanta called him the traitor, the Fallen One. Melanta stayed in the Cage of Suchness and tried to restore the original rules by punishing the residents. Nihilita waited on Windrest Peak for someone who could free the temple. He sent first Raumhilda and then the Traveler, each time lending them the juvenile Watcher Dex.

After his defeat, Melanta understood that "when the divine departs the throne, all creations are free". He admitted that he had acted out of jealousy of Nihilita's freedom and out of hope for his creator's praise, and wondered why she had not asked him to come with her. His own rule-breaking made him self-destruct, and his last words were addressed to Nihilita. Istoria explains that "Watcher" originally meant one who is awakened, and that a Watcher who keeps its eye closed is swallowed by darkness.

71.comment: Temple of Space: Path to the Heavens and the Corridor of Nothingness
71.content:
The Corridor of Nothingness separates the inhabited Hall of Emptiness from the Cage (Atrium) of Suchness at the temple's summit. The only way to an audience with the temple's master, and so the only way out, is to build the Path to the Heavens across the Corridor by giving up all of one's memories and wisdom, so that the temple's truths never reach the mortal world. Walkers on the Path get one last look back at their memories. With Asmoday gone, a path once built does not vanish after use. Melanta, however, destroyed half of the Corridor and cut the Path that Raumhilda had built.

In The Final Judgment, Zeitlind gave up her memories to rebuild the Path. They joined with what was left of her sister's, and the Traveler, crossing it, saw the dreams the two sisters had shared. Back at the sanatorium Zeitlind's memories faded; the Traveler and Paimon told her who she was and that her sister was alive somewhere in the world, and pointed her to her suitcase for clues.

72.comment: Temple of Space: Raumhilda and Zeitlind in the Temple
72.content:
Raumhilda ("Hilda") met Nihilita on a midnight walk while she was staying at the Windrest Peak sanatorium. He entrusted Dex to her and sent her to the temple, where she befriended the residents (she called Istoria "Grandpa"). She also learned painting from Daozi and Bosch. Moved by the residents' suffering, she gave up her memories to build the Path to the Heavens and faced Melanta. They could not agree, and she promised that her younger sister would one day come and defeat him. She left with no memories, and her grave at the sanatorium is empty. Her younger sister Zeitlind later came looking for her, and with the Traveler she freed the temple and paid the same price in memories.

Items Zeitlind brought to say goodbye to her sister were scattered through the halls as "relics". Among them were Kamera photos from Hilda's vacation, the letters the sisters exchanged while Hilda was at the sanatorium, and Hilda's amethyst brooch. Hilda's watermelon still life, "Long Live Life", stays in Luyang Academy at Zeitlind's wish. Zeitlind chose "To be continued" as her own epitaph, echoing the line "One lifetime doesn't count" on her sister's empty grave.

73.comment: Temple of Space: The Damaged Coffin in the Cage of Suchness
73.content:
At the summit of the temple lies a damaged coffin with every trace of its occupant worn away by time. Even so, the Traveler senses that the person who once rested there was the one most important to them. The wiki takes this to be the Traveler's sibling, whom Asmoday took during the Cataclysm. The text urges the Traveler to keep travelling until they meet again. Canon does not show when the sibling was placed there or how they left.

Melanta, asked why a god took the Traveler's sibling, said he did not understand it himself. He had once thought it was punishment for transgressions, but now feared a deeper meaning, and he called the Traveler a being outside the order of the "children of humanity". A note found in the Cage of Suchness, written in both the language of the Andromeda Empire and the local tongue, was left by a self-described novelist who has wandered many worlds. The writer says they slipped out of a "containment facility" after years of tinkering, objects to being locked away without explanation as an illegal entrant, notes having already been paid royalties in Mora by their publisher (Yae Publishing House), and mentions finally working out the ending of "VM" while confined.

74.comment: Temple of Space: Shades' Additions to the Temple
74.content:
Asmoday's rule was pure preservation, but after she vanished her sister Shades softened it. They brought in things they liked and allowed small acts of change. Luyang Academy, a segment of ancient Liyue, grew into a working art school. The Mahavaipulya Chamber filled with new novels by residents. Naberius, Ronova and Istaroth commissioned Venipi to rebuild a Sumeru desert complex from memory, which became the Desert Pavilion. Melanta treated all of this as corruption and punished it until the Traveler restored each hall.

At the Desert Pavilion, Melanta's Suppression-type Keepers and their leader, the Punisher of Gomorrah, kept the residents turned to sand until the Traveler's group defeated them.

75.content:
Teyvat: Teyvat is the world of the story, a planet and the continent on it, where the seven elements (Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro, Pyro, Cryo) flow. It has seven nations, each tied to one element, one ideal and one god of The Seven (the Archons): Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan and Snezhnaya. Above it floats Celestia, seat of the Heavenly Principles, who have ruled the world since conquering it in the distant past. Ordinary people may receive a Vision that lets them wield an element. 500 years ago the fall of the godless underground kingdom Khaenri'ah, the cataclysm, unleashed the Abyss on every nation. That calamity has ended, but peace has not fully returned.

Most people know Teyvat simply as the world of the Archons and Celestia. Few know the truth: the visible sky is a false sky, a shell around the planet, and the true cosmos beyond it is called the sea of stars.

Geography: In official descriptions, Mondstadt lies in the northeast, Liyue is a harbor nation in the east, Inazuma is an isolated archipelago far to the east bordering the Dark Sea, Sumeru is in the west-central part of the continent, Fontaine is a "terrestrial sea" in the center, Natlan lies in the western regions and Snezhnaya is the land of eternal winter in the north. Nod-Krai, an autonomous archipelago under Snezhnaya, sits on the very edge of the continent. Khaenri'ah lay deep underground beneath Sumeru.

Celestia floats over Liyue near Mt. Mingyuan. Teyvat is a planet on the edge of a spiral arm of an unnamed galaxy. The voyager in the artifact text "Deep Gallery's Distant Pact" calls it an unremarkable little world there. Beyond the seven nations lies the "Dark Sea", an umbrella term for unknown lands and waters outside The Seven's rule. Climate follows the nations' elements and gods: green, windy Mondstadt, Liyue's stone forests and mountains, Inazuma's thunderstorms, Sumeru's rainforest and desert, Fontaine's waters, volcanic Natlan, and Snezhnaya's blizzards that can last a month.

Places: Besides the seven nations: Nod-Krai (Snezhnaya's autonomous borderland), fallen Khaenri'ah, Celestia in the sky and the Dark Sea beyond the continent.

| Nation | Element | Ideal | Archon | Main city |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mondstadt | Anemo | Freedom | Barbatos (Venti), first and only | Mondstadt City |
| Liyue | Geo | Contracts | Morax (Zhongli), first and only | Liyue Harbor |
| Inazuma | Electro | Eternity | Baal (Makoto), then Beelzebul (Ei, the Raiden Shogun) | Inazuma City |
| Sumeru | Dendro | Wisdom | Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, then Buer (Nahida) | Sumeru City |
| Fontaine | Hydro | Justice | Egeria, then Focalors (the last) | Court of Fontaine |
| Natlan | Pyro | War | Xbalanque (first), Mavuika (latest) | Stadium of the Sacred Flame |
| Snezhnaya | Cryo | Love | Belyi Tsar, then Vassaga (the Tsaritsa) | Snezhnograd |

Mondstadt is run by the Knights of Favonius, Liyue by the Liyue Qixing, Inazuma by the Shogunate, Sumeru by the Akademiya, Fontaine from Palais Mermonia, Natlan by the Speaker's Chamber and Snezhnaya from the Zapolyarny Palace. Natlan's Archons are mortal humans chosen through the Pilgrimage, so it has had more than two.

People: Humans make up most of Teyvat's population, alongside adepti, spirits, Seelies (the cursed remnants of Angels), vishaps and other elemental creatures, hilichurls and Abyssal monsters. A Vision-holder is called an "allogene", someone said to have the potential to ascend to Celestia and become a god.

Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns who survived the cataclysm are cursed with immortality; Khaenri'ahns of mixed or foreign blood were turned into monsters. Some people come from beyond the false sky and are called Descenders. The Traveler is one: they and their twin arrived during the cataclysm, when Asmoday stopped them from leaving. Irminsul held no record of the Traveler.

Governance: The world order works top-down. The Heavenly Principles rule from Celestia through the Four Shades (Rulers of Life, Death, Time and Space). The Seven govern the nations. Each Archon holds a divine throne in Celestia, made from an elemental Authority taken from a dragon Sovereign, and each received a Gnosis linking them to Celestia.

Celestia also runs a "monitoring cycle" that watches the world and the Shades and sends directives when it decides to intervene. Archons do not choose who gets a Vision; they are only obliged to hand over part of their elemental Authority when one is granted. In punishing whole civilizations that broke its rules, Celestia has driven Celestial Nails into the land (Sal Vindagnyr, Lang-Gan and Hyperborea among them). Since the Hydro Archon's throne was destroyed in Fontaine (4.2), its Authority has returned to the Hydro Sovereign Neuvillette, and only six divine thrones remain. The Heavenly Principles themselves have slept since the cataclysm, because harming Khaenri'ah triggered the Third Descender Saarelainen's curse. Celestia's automatic oversight still runs.

Economy: Mora is the currency accepted everywhere in Teyvat; its item text calls it the one language everybody speaks. It is named after Morax and could only be minted with the Geo Archon's power at Liyue's Golden House, which has stopped minting new Mora since Zhongli gave up the Geo Gnosis.

The Adventurers' Guild, which posts work in every nation, originates from Snezhnaya, and its Katheryne receptionists are confirmed Snezhnayan puppets. Trade runs between the great ports (Liyue Harbor, Mondstadt's Dornman Port, Sumeru's Port Ormos, among others). Snezhnaya is the most technologically advanced nation, with large factories and the Fatui's advanced weaponry. Nod-Krai has a reputation as a place to get rich, but it is lawless apart from the Voynich Guild.

History: Teyvat's history in broad strokes:
- **The Old World:** dragons ruled under the Seven Sovereigns and their king, Nibelung, who raised Three Moons from the planet's crust.
- **The conquest:** the Heavenly Principles came from the stars, defeated the dragons, took their Authorities and built a human "unified civilization" guided by Angels.
- **The war of funerary flame, about 6,000 years ago:** Nibelung returned with the Abyss. The war shattered that civilization and two of the moons, and all history from before it was banned.
- **The Archon War, about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago:** gods fought for seven thrones, and The Seven and their nations emerged.
- **The cataclysm, 500 years ago:** Khaenri'ah fell and the Abyss spread across all seven nations.
- **The present:** the Traveler's journey through the seven nations in search of their twin.

In the cataclysm Makoto, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, Egeria and the Belyi Tsar died and were succeeded. Mavuika sealed her life in the Sacred Flame and returned 500 years later. The Abyss Order and the Fatui both arose in answer to Celestia's actions. Liyue Harbor was founded about 3,700 years ago and Barbatos rose about 2,600 years ago; the Archon War ended about 2,000 years ago when the last throne was claimed. See the master timeline entity for detail.

Atmosphere: Most people live ordinary lives under their nation's god, treat Celestia as distant and holy, and never question the sky. Statues of the Seven stand across the land. Ruins of older civilizations are everywhere, often unexplained. Since the moon changed and the Nails began to glow, people have noticed more and more signs in the sky.

Dangers: Common hazards include hilichurl camps, slimes, Treasure Hoarders, rogue Ruin machines, the Fatui's schemes and the Abyss Order. Corrupted ley lines and Abyssal corruption remain, along with hostile climates: Dragonspine's cold, Sumeru's desert and Snezhnaya's blizzards. Cosmic threats: the Abyss, a destructive force from the sea of stars that has annihilated other worlds, including the Traveler's own, strains constantly to enter Teyvat. Alice and Nicole both warned that Teyvat's borders had grown fragile and that the world became easier to detect from outside after the Nod-Krai crisis.

Travel: People travel overland by road and caravan, and by ship between ports. Inazuma was closed for years by the Sakoku Decree. Snezhnaya can only be crossed by those who can survive the cold. Celestia is unreachable except by those who ascend, and Khaenri'ah is no longer reachable. Gameplay note: teleport waypoints and Statues of the Seven are a game convenience. In-world, walking, horses, boats and wind gliders are what people actually use.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Archon Quest is in Snezhnaya (Chapter VII). The Heavenly Principles still sleep. The Tsaritsa's Fatui hold six of the seven Gnoses and are openly preparing to challenge Celestia. The Frost Moon has returned to Teyvat's sky.

In 7.1 the Tsaritsa outmaneuvered the Shade Rhinedottir, and Celestia stripped Ronova of the Authority of Death for abusing it. Pierro's group then defeated Ronova. In her last act, the mortally wounded Ronova made the Celestial Nail over the Cryo Dragon's corpse crumble, threatening to spread Holy Soil across Teyvat. Every other Nail began to shine a strange light into the sky, visible to people everywhere.

Earlier changes still stand. Irminsul was burned by Nahida in Luna VII (6.6) after Dottore corrupted it, and the Aaru system has taken over its role. The Pyro Gnosis vanished in that fire. Six divine thrones remain. With the Curse of Death lifted, the Fatui's anti-Celestia weapon project Mistilteinn is no longer held back. Nicole has warned that Teyvat is now more detectable from outside.

76.content:
Each of Teyvat's seven nations worships the Archon of one element, and that Archon's ideal shapes its government: Mondstadt (Anemo, freedom), Liyue (Geo, contracts), Inazuma (Electro, eternity), Sumeru (Dendro, wisdom), Fontaine (Hydro, justice), Natlan (Pyro, war) and Snezhnaya (Cryo, love). The nations were founded after the Archon War about 2,000 years ago, when the winning gods shaped their lands with their elemental power. Snezhnaya counts as independent, like Mondstadt, and it administers the autonomous borderland of Nod-Krai.

Five of the original Seven have died over the centuries. The original Seven were friendly and often gathered in Liyue for drinks. Inazuma's, Sumeru's, Fontaine's and Snezhnaya's first Archons all died around the cataclysm. Fontaine's Hydro throne no longer exists, and Natlan's Archons are mortals chosen through the Pilgrimage.

77.content: Celestia is a floating cluster of landmasses in the sky over Liyue, near Mt. Mingyuan. It has a great central spire, outer rocks linked by a ring, and rivers that pour off its edges and fade into nothing as they fall. People believe heroes ascend there to become gods. It is home to the Heavenly Principles and the meeting place of the Four Shades (Asmoday has been absent since the cataclysm). The Angels lived there until they were cast out. Venti claims its water tastes foul and its fruit is bland.

78.content: The "Dark Sea" is the umbrella name for everything beyond the continent and outside The Seven's rule, landmasses included. Gods defeated in the Archon War who refused the new order fled there. Enkanomiya, though it lies directly beneath Watatsumi Island, counts as Dark Sea because The Seven have no jurisdiction over it. Inazuma borders the Dark Sea.

79.content:
Teyvat once had three moons, raised by the dragon king Nibelung from the planet's crust: the Eternal, Frost and Iridescent Moons. Long ago the spirits of the frozen north called these three silver lights "Dilimbabbar", and by them the seasons and years were first counted. In the war of funerary flame the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were shattered and the Frost Moon was flung outside the false sky. For about 6,000 years people saw only a projected false moon, the shadowmoon. In Song of the Welkin Moon Act VIII (6.3) the Frost Moon was pulled back through the false sky and now orbits inside it, with Columbina as its goddess, and people noticed the moon looked different. The shadowmoon later fell apart during a Lantern Rite.

Fragments of the Eternal Moon became faintly visible from Natlan (5.3) after Mavuika's strike against the Abyss broke the sky. Mavuika described the event to the public as an "astronomical anomaly". The far side of the Frost Moon was rebuilt as a huge cannon in Nibelung's war. Dragon research stations from Project Moongazer still stand on it, and the twins' spaceship was hidden there.

80.content: The sky seen from Teyvat is a false sky: a physical shell the Heavenly Principles wrapped around the planet to hide it from the cosmos, built from the dragon Lusalim's "lunar veil" technology. From inside it projects an ordinary-looking sky. The book "Before Sun and Moon" calls it the eggshell of Phanes; some see it as a cage. It has split open only a few times: when Surtalogi sent Skirk through, during Mavuika's strike in Natlan, and when Dottore tore it open as the Heretic of the False Moon (which let the Frost Moon return).

81.content:
Before the Archons, Teyvat belonged to the dragons. The Seven Sovereigns divided it under Nibelung; Natlantea, for example, was the Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl's land. After the Heavenly Principles conquered the dragons, Angels guided a unified human civilization with several realms: Arcadia (Windrest Peak), Sal Vindagnyr (Dragonspine), Lang-Gan (now the Chasm), Delphi Pytho (present-day Inazuma), the harbor of Ys (now under Sumeru's sands), Patraipolis, Meropis (Fontaine) and golden Hyperborea (Snezhnaya). Nod-Krai, then called Nephilheim, was made from material left over from the moons' creation. The war of funerary flame destroyed this order. Afterward new god-kingdoms arose, such as Decarabian's Mondstadt, the Guili Assembly, Remuria, Byakuyakoku/Enkanomiya and King Deshret's desert realm.

The voyager of "Deep Gallery's Distant Pact" describes the change as she saw it. When she returned, the bones of the earth were bound beneath fourfold shackles. The sky's white radiance had been split into seven fixed hues. The "Winged One" now sat on the throne that ruled the three moons.

82.content: Khaenri'ah was a nation built by humans with no god at all, deep underground beneath Sumeru. People from the seven nations joined it over the millennia. 500 years ago, monsters bearing the Abyss's power, created by the alchemist Rhinedottir, poured out of it across Teyvat. The Heavenly Principles and The Seven destroyed Khaenri'ah for its use of the Art of Khemia and Abyssal power. Its surviving pure-blooded people were cursed with immortality, and those of mixed or foreign blood were turned into monsters. The bitterness this left gave rise to the Abyss Order and the Fatui.

83.content: Mora is Teyvat's universal currency. A loading screen says none dispute its value. Mora is also a catalyst for physical transformation, which is why crafters use it. It is named after Morax, and only the Geo Archon's power could mint it at the Golden House in Liyue, which has minted no new Mora since Zhongli surrendered his Gnosis.

84.comment: Teyvat: The 7.1 Crisis of the Nails
84.content: At the end of Chapter VII Act IV (7.1) Ronova had lost her Authority and was mortally wounded. She teleported to the Celestial Nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse, once Hyperborea's Nail, and fused the life-altering substance Eitr with it. The Nail crumbled, threatening to unleash Holy Soil across all of Teyvat, land unfit for human life. Every other Nail across the world then began casting a strange light into the sky, and ordinary people saw it at once. Zhongli and Mavuika went on high alert. The outcome is unresolved as of 7.1.

85.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End
85.content:
The Sea of Flowers at the End (also: Sea of Flowers at the End, Sea of Flowers of the End): The Sea of Flowers at the End is a place where Inteyvat flowers, the national flower of Khaenri'ah, bloom in full. The Traveler's sibling found it at the end of their long journey. The Traveler had once said they wished to find such a place in the universe, so its discovery moved the sibling to stop travelling with the Traveler and take up Teyvat's affairs.

It is not a place the player can visit. Everything known comes from the sibling's own words to the Traveler during the Sumeru-set Archon Quest World-Order Narration.

The sibling frames the place as something they cannot quite explain: they offer it to the Traveler as proof that they still remember the old wish, while admitting they do not know how to face the Traveler as the conflict goes on.

Description: The sea is made of Inteyvat flowers: five-petalled blooms, four white petals and one pale blue. The name is the sibling's, repeated in quotation marks as a proper name for the place.

Inteyvat once bloomed all over Khaenri'ah and lasts only about two weeks before wilting. Taken out of Khaenri'ah, the petals reportedly harden and soften again only when the flower returns to its home soil, so it is a symbol of a wanderer far from home. This is Dainsleif's account in Memories of Inteyvat. The flower is also what Lumine wears in her hair.

History: During their travels between worlds, the Traveler told their sibling they wanted to find a place in the universe where Inteyvat flowers were in full bloom. At the end of the sibling's journey across Teyvat, the sibling found such a place: the Sea of Flowers at the End.

The sibling tells this to the Traveler in the Sumeru Archon Quest, after the Traveler asks why the two cannot keep travelling together. The sibling asks whether the Traveler really thinks it a coincidence that such a place suddenly appeared before them, and says they miss the Traveler too.

The sibling places the conversation in the middle of an ongoing war and their search for a final answer, and says that in this state they do not always know how to face themselves, let alone their own sibling. The Sea of Flowers is thus offered as a memory of shared wishes, not as a refuge the Traveler can be taken to. The place's names in other languages (Chinese Zhongjing de Huahai, Japanese Hate no Hana no Umi) both mean roughly 'the final / farthest sea of flowers'.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible and not visited by anyone shown in game as of 7.1. The Traveler has heard of it only through the sibling.

86.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End: Sea of Flowers and the sibling
86.content: In World-Order Narration the Traveler's sibling names the Sea of Flowers at the End as the place where they stopped their journey, and links it to the Traveler's old wish to find a world where the Inteyvat flower bloomed in full. The sibling does not say where it is or what is there beyond the flowers.

87.comment: The Sea of Flowers at the End: Inteyvat
87.content: Inteyvat is the national flower of Khaenri'ah, with four white petals and one pale blue petal. Dainsleif tells of it wilting in two weeks and hardening when taken away from Khaenri'ah. The Traveler says the same flowers grow in their homeland; Lumine wears one in her hair. Emilie, a modern Teyvat resident, had never heard of it before being told by the Traveler.

88.content:
Tletl Ilhuicatl (also: Tletl Ilhuicatl realm layout): Tletl Ilhuicatl is the Natlan-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 5.3. The game places it high above a sea of clouds, where towering peaks bask in scorching sunlight and the air is full of endless heat. The name is Nahuatl, from words for 'fire' and 'sky'.

It is unlocked by buying the Scroll of the Fiery Firmament from Tubby at the Realm Depot after finishing Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (the layout's own page names Home of the Hot Springs instead). Its mansion is the Natlan Dwelling: "Lofty Tower"; the four areas are Firecage, Blazebelt, Flamecrest and Sunridge.

The signature feature is travel by hot air balloon. A balloon stop is described in-game as a resting place formed by Adeptal Energy and a landing ground for Phlogiston Hot Air Balloons, the favoured transport of Natlan's tribes.

Geography: Sunlit peaks and ridges over clouds, with long cliff-side terraces. Firecage and Blazebelt share an island at different heights; Flamecrest sits at the lowest elevation; Sunridge is a long strip overlooked by a cliff face.

Halberd-Crest Birds fly around the layout; they are scenery and cannot be attacked.

Places: Firecage (Trust Rank 1): the lower starting area, with a Sub-Space Waypoint on the cliff above it and a seat beside a lantern on the westernmost cliff. Blazebelt (Rank 5): overlooks Firecage and has a balloon platform to Flamecrest. Flamecrest (Rank 7): a long, thin area; balloons run to Blazebelt (through a short canyon) and to Sunridge. Sunridge (Rank 9): long and thin, reached by balloon from Flamecrest.

Each area has the same 16,000 load cap as the other layouts.

Travel: Entered through the Serenitea Pot gadget once the scroll is used; inside, the hot air balloons run between areas. Chubby, who brought the scroll as a souvenir from Natlan, appears at one unlocked area on Fridays to Sundays.

Atmosphere: Hot, bright and open, with balloons and birds drifting overhead. It evokes Natlan's tribes and Phlogiston travel, but no war or Archon trial exists here.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 unchanged since 5.3; it remains quest-gated through the scroll.

89.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Scroll of the Fiery Firmament
89.content: The item that unlocks Tletl Ilhuicatl: a woven scroll from Natlan depicting its landscapes, brought back by Chubby as a souvenir. It is bought from Tubby in the Realm Depot after Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn.

90.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Phlogiston Hot Air Balloon Stops
90.content: In-game map text describes the stops as resting places formed by Adeptal Energy, landing grounds for the Phlogiston Hot Air Balloons favoured by Natlan's tribes. Players ride them to other areas of the realm.

91.content: The four areas of Tletl Ilhuicatl: Firecage (Trust Rank 1), Blazebelt (5), Flamecrest (7) and Sunridge (9).

92.comment: Tletl Ilhuicatl: Natlan Dwelling: Lofty Tower
92.content: The mansion furnishing supplied with Tletl Ilhuicatl; the game gives no lore beyond its name.

93.content:
Tower of Radiant Light (also: Brilliant Light Tower): The Tower of Radiant Light is a large tower in Luyang Academy, the painting gallery of the Temple of Space. The Traveler climbs it during the quest Long Live Life, in the effort to restore the Academy.

Its name is rendered as 明光楼 in Chinese, which translates literally as Tower of Brilliant Light.

Geography: The tower stands within the Liyue-styled compound of Luyang Academy, which is built on a small island. The painter Daozi says the direct path to it is barred, so the party must approach through the Abode of Resplendent Talent.

In the quest the final approach is made in a painted world, at a moment when ink is chasing the party. A lift carries the Traveler to the top, where the other side of an important painting can be reached from inside the tower.

History: Daozi, freed from a painting early in Long Live Life, explains that the Academy cannot be restored until a particular painting is completed. Its title, as he gives it, is "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White", and in his words it should be possible to complete the missing part of it in the Tower of Radiant Light.

The party reaches the tower after being led into an ink trap by a figure who falsely claimed to be the painter Escher. They flee through re-projected paintings with Dex's help until a bridge painting is destroyed and they drop to the ground near the tower. At the top they come to the painting from its other side, and Daozi is waiting there. He then adds the finishing stroke that connects the set of paintings and opens the way to the Pavilion of Paintings at the centre of the Academy. Plucking the star there unrolls a great scroll, reveals the whole Academy and frees its inhabitants from the ink.

During the climb the game limits the party to the Traveler, restricts movement to a fixed side-on or top-down view and disables combat talents. Daozi attributes the ink and the false Escher to Melanta, the Watcher who punishes people by sealing them in paintings.

Atmosphere: Ink, mist and Liyue-style halls; the sense of climbing out of a painted world while a dark flood presses behind.

Dangers: Ink blots and flowing ink are harmful to touch, and the Domain Keepers of the Temple of Space guard the Academy. Neither is tied specifically to the tower beyond the chase that leads to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Academy is restored and its painters are free; the tower has no further role in the story.

94.comment: Tower of Radiant Light: Hall of Painted Worlds
94.content: Daozi's plan for restoring Luyang Academy depends on a painting named "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White", which he says is Inazuman in its taste for names. The tower is where its missing part was expected to be completed.

95.content:
Twinning Isle: Twinning Isle is a limited-time island group in the northeast of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. In the 1.6 Midsummer Island Adventure it was a cluster of fog-wrapped islets and a central stage with a samurai puppet; in 2.8 Summertime Odyssey it held a castle of Night Ravens connected with Fischl's imagination.

The Immernachtreich of the 2.8 event is Fischl's imagined realm, and the Night Raven castle on Twinning Isle is where the event placed it on the map.

Geography: In 1.6 the main island held a teleport waypoint, a cave beneath it with notes for the quest A Trip Through Fog and Wind, wind currents to its heights and Hymnal Rings; a south island, southeast islets, a northeast rock with a cave, and a Nameless Islet reachable only through sea fog completed the group.

Between 10:00 and 14:00 the sea fog could be pierced by following wind lines, which led to the Nameless Islet with a mural and five chests. In event Stage 2 a Central Platform appeared southwest of the main island: a large stage with a Maguu Kenki at its centre, which could be fought after the Dodo-King storyline.

The 2.8 map built a castle on the isle in three stages. Before Immernachtreich Apokalypse was cleared, notices said the Twilight Theater's latest work was still in development and a bridge to a tower was closed for construction. Nachtraben Airlines and the Raven Forum are among the fixtures.

People: In 2.8 the isle's residents are Night Ravens: talkative and theatrical workers, guards, storytellers and a squire who hopes to become a knight like Sir Oz. They speak of the Traveler as having the Prinzessin's eyes, meaning Fischl's.

History: The Maguu Kenki on the Central Platform was, per the archipelago timeline, stolen by an Inazuma pirate crew about 500 years ago and later protected the islanders until it was damaged and went inactive. That crew's boat had split in two, and one group drifted to the southeast of Twinning Isle.

Immernachtreich Apokalypse (the fourth act of the 2.8 event) takes the party into a mirage of Fischl's imagination, in which a narrator recounts her life and raven statues stand for her kingdom's citizens. Back on the isle, Fischl is glad to have faced her insecurities. At the castle's top the Traveler and Paimon try to contact Venti, and an unknown voice intercepts the call.

Dangers: In 2.8, hilichurls, slimes, a Pyro Abyss Mage and Eye of the Storm and Stonehide Lawachurl elites. In 1.6, Pyro Whopperflowers, Mitachurls, a Cryo Abyss Mage, Dendro slimes and the Maguu Kenki on the platform.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; limited to the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.
